findings.issue_text: P1: Crash when destinationCalendar is an empty array in EventManager.ts (~118) — destructuring yields undefined and .integration throws TypeError; optional chaining was dropped, crashing booking creation for users with Google Meet location and no destination calendar

P1: Google deleteEvent/updateEvent fallback lookup broken in CalendarService.ts (~255, ~315) — when externalCalendarId is falsy, it searches for externalId === undefined, never matches, so selectedCalendar is always undefined; deleteEvent calls API with calendarId undefined and updateEvent no longer falls back to booking's destination calendar

P2: Google createEvent silently creates events on 'primary' calendar (~150) when destinationCalendar has no entry matching credentialId (stale/legacy data or deleted credential), placing event on wrong calendar with no error

P2: In handleNewBooking.ts (~1090), when neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null and ?.push is a no-op, silently dropping COLLECTIVE team members' destination calendars; should be evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]

P2: In EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (~493-550), missing credential leaves credential undefined and updateEvent still called, throwing inside getCalendar; the throw escapes to outer catch so all remaining calendar references' updates are skipped and reported as failure (appName: 'none')

P2: In EventManager.ts (~166-175), externalCalendarId no longer persisted when creation failed — booking reference comes from createEvent result instead of evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId, so on Google 404 path no usable calendar reference is stored, breaking later reschedules/cancels

P2: loadUsers in handleNewBooking.ts (~722-765) dropped organization select from dynamic-user query, so downstream org-dependent logic reading user.organization gets undefined; also converts all unknown errors into HttpError 400 'Unable to load users' without logging the original error

P3: Collective booking uses destinationCalendar[0] as 'main host' for organizer email (~100) — order-dependent and not guaranteed to be the organizer's calendar if an eventType-level calendar exists for a different user

Inverted billing-condition logic in org creation: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ternary flips slug persistence, so with billing disabled orgs get no slug and with billing enabled slugs are reserved pre-payment enabling slug squatting (organizations/create.handler.ts:148-154)

Google updateEvent: when externalCalendarId is undefined, destinationCalendar find can never match, so update is issued with a broken/undefined calendarId instead of falling back to destinationCalendar.externalId (CalendarService.ts:253)

Google deleteEvent: tautological lookup comparing cal.externalId against the externalCalendarId parameter itself; when externalCalendarId is falsy calendarId is undefined and legacy bookings' events are not deleted, leaving orphaned events (CalendarService.ts:312-315)

Credentials fetched from DB by raw credentialId in createAllCalendarEvents and handleCancelBooking without validating ownership against the booking organizer/hosts, allowing cross-tenant credential use (EventManager.ts:~348-370, handleCancelBooking.ts:~424-432)

Collective non-credentialId fallback branch calls createEvent without externalId, causing Google createEvent to fall back to 'primary' instead of the destination secondary calendar, placing events on the wrong calendar (CalendarManager.ts:230, CalendarService.ts:145)

Only the first destination calendar is persisted to the booking; other collective members' calendars are never stored, so cancellation/reschedule never updates or deletes their calendar events (handleNewBooking.ts:~1871-1875)
Organizer email is set from destinationCalendar[0] regardless of integration; a non-Google calendar first in the list sets an invalid organizer email on the Google event (CalendarService.ts:100-124)

handleCancelBooking DB credential fetch by booking reference credentialId does not verify it belongs to bookingToDelete.user, potentially deleting events on another user's calendar (destructive version of the ownership-validation gap)

N+1 DB query: per-destination credential fetch inside loop in packages/core/EventManager.ts ~line 345 (createAllCalendarEvents) — individual prisma.credential.findUnique awaited per destination, should be batched with findMany

N+1 DB query: per-reference credential fetch inside loop in packages/core/EventManager.ts ~line 500 (updateAllCalendarEvents) — sequential prisma.credential.findUnique per calendar reference, should be batched
N+1 DB query in cancel handler: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~line 425 performs prisma.credential.findUnique per booking reference, should be batched with findMany

Sequential event creation across destination calendars in packages/core/EventManager.ts ~line 340 (createAllCalendarEvents) — createEvent awaited serially per destination instead of Promise.all, increasing wall time for collective bookings

P1 Crash: `.integration` accessed on possibly-undefined first element — when `destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws TypeError, breaking every booking with Google Meet location and no destination calendar (packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119)

P0 Delete/update falls back to wrong calendar (dead-code fallback) — when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === undefined)` can never match, so delete/update targets `primary` or fails, potentially deleting/updating events in the wrong calendar (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts deleteEvent:315, updateEvent:255-257)

P2 External webhook payload shape drift — BOOKING_REJECTED webhook's `destinationCalendar` now sends empty array instead of null/object, an undocumented payload-shape change to an externally consumed boundary with no versioning (apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249)

P2 Organization creation slug logic inverted — new code sets `slug` only when billing is enabled, whereas old code set it when billing was disabled, so with billing disabled the org is created with no slug, breaking org URL resolution (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-152)

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Crash when destinationCalendar is an empty array in EventManager.ts (~118) — destructuring yields undefined and .integration throws TypeError; optional chaining was dropped, crashing booking creation for users with Google Meet location and no destination calendar

P1: Google deleteEvent/updateEvent fallback lookup broken in CalendarService.ts (~255, ~315) — when externalCalendarId is falsy, it searches for externalId === undefined, never matches, so selectedCalendar is always undefined; deleteEvent calls API with calendarId undefined and updateEvent no longer falls back to booking's destination calendar

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the fallback logic for `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` was changed from using the event’s destination calendar to a `.find()` that compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy:

- `updateEvent`: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
- `deleteEvent`: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/falsy, this searches for `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will not match real calendar externalIds, so it returns `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` is populated. This removes the prior fallback behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can lead to an undefined calendarId being used (or at least not using the intended destination calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Google createEvent silently creates events on 'primary' calendar (~150) when destinationCalendar has no entry matching credentialId (stale/legacy data or deleted credential), placing event on wrong calendar with no error

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendarId is now chosen by `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then used as `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` (see added logic around `selectedCalendar` and `events.insert`). If `destinationCalendar` is non-empty but has no entry matching the passed `credentialId` (stale/legacy data, deleted credential, mismatch), `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the event is inserted into the user's `primary` calendar without error. Previously, a stale `destinationCalendar.externalId` would be used directly and could trigger a 404 that was caught/returned as undefined; this change can instead silently create the event on the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In handleNewBooking.ts (~1090), when neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null and ?.push is a no-op, silently dropping COLLECTIVE team members' destination calendars; should be evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team event types, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, this optional-chaining push is a no-op, so any `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from other users (via `teamMemberPromises`) are silently dropped. This is a correctness issue in the new array-based destinationCalendar logic introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (~493-550), missing credential leaves credential undefined and updateEvent still called, throwing inside getCalendar; the throw escapes to outer catch so all remaining calendar references' updates are skipped and reported as failure (appName: 'none')
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that when a referenced credential is missing, `credential` remains undefined but `updateEvent` is still invoked, leading to a throw/runtime failure. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (undefined credential passed to `updateEvent` when `reference.credentialId` is set but lookup fails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In EventManager.ts (~166-175), externalCalendarId no longer persisted when creation failed — booking reference comes from createEvent result instead of evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId, so on Google 404 path no usable calendar reference is stored, breaking later reschedules/cancels

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always returns an `EventResult` that includes `externalId` (the optional param) and `credentialId`, even when the underlying calendar creation fails (including the Google 404 catch path where it returns `undefined` for `createdEvent` but still returns the wrapper result). In `EventManager`, `externalCalendarId` is now taken from `result.externalId`, and `createAllCalendarEvents` passes `destination.externalId` into `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for the credential-linked destination calendars. Therefore, even on the Google 404 path, a reference can still carry the external calendar id via `result.externalId`. The finding’s claim that no usable calendar reference is stored specifically due to the 404 path is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email is set from destinationCalendar[0] regardless of integration; a non-Google calendar first in the list sets an invalid organizer email on the Google event (CalendarService.ts:100-124)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent()`, the organizer attendee email is derived from `mainHostDestinationCalendar`, which is set to the *first* element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). This value is then used for `payload.attendees[0].email` (`email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`). However, the calendar actually used for insertion is selected by matching `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). With the new array semantics (and code that appends team members’ destination calendars), the first destination calendar can belong to a different integration/credential than the Google credential being used, causing Google event creation to use an incorrect/non-email `externalId` as the organizer attendee email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Only first destination calendar connected to booking record — collective events risk orphaned calendar events for other hosts (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1871-1876)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `evt.destinationCalendar` can contain multiple calendars for COLLECTIVE team events (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`), but when persisting the booking it only connects the first one: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (handleNewBooking.ts ~1871-1876). That’s an implementation inconsistency/limitation: the booking record will not reflect additional host destination calendars. However, the claim that this will “orphan” other hosts’ calendar events is not directly verifiable from this diff because other lifecycle operations (update/delete) were also changed to iterate over `_calendar` references, which likely remain the source of truth for managing created events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Google createEvent silently falls back to 'primary' on credential mismatch — event created on wrong calendar while externalId points at intended calendar, causing later update/delete to target wrong event (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~146-149)

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent, the target calendar is chosen by finding a destinationCalendar entry matching the passed credentialId; if none is found, it silently falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Meanwhile EventManager passes `destination.externalId` into CalendarManager.createEvent, which returns it as `result.externalId`, and EventManager then stores/uses `result.externalId` as `externalCalendarId` for later update/delete. This creates a verifiable mismatch scenario: event may be created on `primary` while the stored externalCalendarId still points to the intended destination calendar, causing later update/delete to target the wrong calendar/event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Serialized per-destination event creation without isolation of partial failures — DB fetch error aborts remaining destinations leaving partially-created events, plus latency regression vs Promise.all (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~341-370)

adjudication.rationale: In `createAllCalendarEvents` the new per-destination `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and `await createEvent(...)` inline (no per-iteration try/catch). This serializes creation across destinations (latency regression vs the previous `Promise.all(...)` path) and introduces a new failure point (DB fetch) that, if it throws, will abort the loop after some destinations may already have been created—i.e., partial completion without isolation/compensation. The diff does not show any cleanup/rollback strategy for already-created events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: handleCancelBooking pushes raw promises including undefined into apiDeletes — unobserved deletions multiplied per calendar reference, increasing silent orphan risk (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~486)

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking, apiDeletes can receive non-Promise values due to optional chaining on calendar?.deleteEvent(...). In the recurring-event branch, `const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` will be `undefined` if `getCalendar(credential)` returns undefined, and that `undefined` is pushed into `apiDeletes` (new loop around multiple references increases occurrences). In the non-recurring branch it also does `apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...) as Promise<unknown>)`, which will still push `undefined` at runtime if `calendar` is undefined. If later code does `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)`, `undefined` entries resolve immediately, silently masking skipped deletions and increasing orphaned external events risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition inverted in organizations/create.handler.ts:148-152, flipping org slug assignment behavior (requestedSlug now set only when billing enabled) — unrelated accidental change

adjudication.rationale: In `organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition for assigning `slug` inside `organization.create` was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts when the slug is written. This is a concrete behavioral flip visible in the diff and can change organization slug persistence behavior depending on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible TypeError in EventManager.ts:118-120: destructuring empty destinationCalendar array yields undefined, and .integration access crashes event creation

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array (which the diff now frequently sets to `[]`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and `.integration` will throw a TypeError. Previously the code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and would not crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google deleteEvent fails when externalCalendarId undefined: find matches externalId===undefined, calendarId becomes undefined instead of falling back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed their fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, this `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` instead of falling back to the event’s destination calendar (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This matches the finding: delete/update can target an undefined calendarId rather than the intended destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google updateEvent same bug: when externalCalendarId falsy, selectedCalendar is undefined where previously event's own destination calendar was used

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback logic for `selectedCalendar` was changed from `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), this now searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `undefined`/`null`), which will typically return `undefined` instead of using the event’s destination calendar. This matches the finding: the previous behavior used the event's destination calendar, the new code commonly yields `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking only connects destinationCalendar[0] to the Booking record; other hosts' calendar links in collective events are lost, breaking reschedule/cancel flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `evt.destinationCalendar` can contain multiple calendars for COLLECTIVE events (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), but when persisting the Booking it still only connects the first calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`). That means the Booking record itself cannot represent multiple destination calendars. However, the diff also refactors cancel/reschedule/update logic to operate over `_calendar` references (now treated as arrays via `filter(...)` loops), so the claim that reschedule/cancel flows are definitively broken by this is not directly verifiable from the diff. The issue is real as a data-model/behavior mismatch (multi-DC in event vs single DC on Booking), but the specific “breaking reschedule/cancel flows” part is not proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-Google calendar services (Lark, Office365, lib CalendarService) blindly use destinationCalendar[0] without checking it matches their integration/credential, potentially creating events in wrong integration's calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now loops over *each* destination calendar, selecting a matching credential per destination and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts). However, non-Google calendar services still derive the target calendar solely from the first element: e.g. Lark uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;` in `createEvent`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Office365 uses `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` to build the URL (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). BaseCalendarService similarly filters by the first destination (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). With multiple destination calendars (e.g. collective team booking where `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), these implementations can create/update/delete on the wrong calendar because they do not select the destination calendar corresponding to the current credential/integration being processed (unlike Google, which now selects by `credentialId`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential-from-DB fallback logic duplicated three times (EventManager createAll/updateAll, handleCancelBooking); cancel copy omits include:{app} handling — should be extracted helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows credential-from-DB fallback logic implemented in multiple places: in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` and `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (both call `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and then reconstruct a `CredentialWithAppName`), and again in `handleCancelBooking` (calls `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId }})`). This is duplicated, and the `handleCancelBooking` version is less feature-complete (no `include: { app }`), which is a maintainability/consistency concern suitable for extraction into a helper. However, it’s not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone because `handleCancelBooking` appears to need only a `Credential` for `getCalendar`, not an `appName`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: teamDestinationCalendars.push inside concurrent Promise.all makes array order depend on promise resolution, so index 0 'mainHost' calendar may not be the organizer's

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar)` occurs **before any `await`** inside the `async` mapper passed to `users.slice(1).map(...)`. That means the `push` happens synchronously during the `map` loop, in the same order as `users.slice(1)`, not in Promise resolution order. Also, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized with `[eventType.destinationCalendar]` or `[organizerUser.destinationCalendar]` (so the organizer/eventType calendar is index 0), and only afterwards `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` appends team calendars, preserving index 0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: eventType.schedulingType compared with raw 'COLLECTIVE' string literal instead of SchedulingType enum, weakening type boundary

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, the diff replaces enum comparisons with raw string literals: `['COLLECTIVE','ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(eventType.schedulingType)` and later `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. This is diff-grounded and does weaken type safety/compile-time guarantees versus using `SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE` / `SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` (as the prior code did). However, since Prisma enum values are runtime strings, this is not a clearly verifiable functional bug from the diff alone—more a maintainability/type-boundary concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loadUsers rewrite drops organization.slug select and swallows errors into generic 500 — unrelated churn increasing regression surface

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the `loadUsers` rewrite changes the Prisma `select` for the `findMany` branch and removes the previously-selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` entirely. It also introduces a broad `try/catch` that converts non-`HttpError`/non-Prisma-known errors into a generic `HttpError` 500 (`"Unable to load users"`), which can obscure underlying failures. While the diff doesn’t show downstream usage proving a definite runtime break, this is real, diff-grounded behavioral/API-shape churn that increases regression surface and reduces error specificity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook evt objects now send destinationCalendar: [] instead of null, breaking downstream consumers distinguishing 'no calendar'; normalizing on null recommended

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes webhook-related payload expectations from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []` (e.g., `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` updated to expect `[]`). Multiple event builders now set `destinationCalendar` to an empty array when no selection exists (e.g., `bookingReminder.ts` and `packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts` use `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`). While the diff doesn’t prove downstream breakage, it does show an externally-visible shape/semantic change (null vs empty array) and even inconsistency (some places still set `null`, e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`), so the compatibility concern is grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant no-op find predicate in Google update/delete: find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId is an identity lookup that does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `.deleteEvent`, the fallback path uses `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case the predicate compares against `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`, meaning `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` rather than selecting a meaningful destination calendar. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff (the find is effectively useless in the fallback branch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~line 253-256): fallback when externalCalendarId is falsy compares cal.externalId === undefined, so selectedCalendar is always undefined (previously fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId); booking reference updates lacking externalCalendarId target an undefined calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback path when `externalCalendarId` is falsy was changed to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, this compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, so it will almost always return `undefined` (unless a calendar has an undefined externalId), whereas the previous code fell back to the event’s destination calendar. This makes `selectedCalendar` undefined in the common case where booking references don’t carry `externalCalendarId`, and risks updating the wrong calendar (or failing) depending on how the subsequent API call handles an undefined `calendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~line 312-315): same broken pattern — with no externalCalendarId the find never matches, calendarId is undefined, so old events are never deleted from the correct calendar (orphaned events on cancel/reschedule-merge)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, both updateEvent and deleteEvent now derive the calendar ID like `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `find` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to `undefined`, so it will not match any real calendar and returns `undefined`. That makes the computed calendarId undefined (or forces a fallback like "primary" if used later), so deletions/updates can target the wrong calendar or fail to delete the originally-created event—consistent with orphaned events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: core/EventManager.ts ~line 117: crash when destinationCalendar is null or empty array — mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and reading .integration throws TypeError, hard-failing Google Meet booking creation (old code used optional chaining)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Meet fallback check. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this throws a TypeError. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and would not crash. The diff also introduces call sites that can produce `destinationCalendar: []` (e.g. webhook.e2e.ts, bookingReminder.ts, payments/webhook.ts), making this crash reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizations/create.handler.ts ~line 148-152: inverted billing logic — ternary rewrite flips both conditions, so with billing enabled org gets slug directly (bypassing billing gate) and requestedSlug isn't recorded; with billing disabled slug is silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts the spread condition for setting `slug` was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips the behavior: when team billing is disabled the org will no longer get `slug`, and when enabled it will now get `slug` directly. That is a real behavioral change consistent with the finding’s core claim (though the diff still records `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled via `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (~line 500-530): updateEvent can be called with undefined credential if credentialId exists but credential isn't in calendarCredentials and DB fetch fails or lacks app.slug, throwing and aborting updates for remaining calendar references

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (refactored to handle multiple calendar references), when a reference has credentialId it sets `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]` and, if not found, tries `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and only reconstructs `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug`. Regardless of whether either lookup succeeds, it then unconditionally executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));`. If both lookups fail (or DB fetch returns without `app.slug`), `credential` remains undefined and `updateEvent` is invoked with undefined, which can throw and cause the outer try/catch to abort processing of remaining references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts ~line 1089-1091: evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType nor organizer has one, so optional-chained push is a no-op and collective team members' destination calendars are silently dropped (no calendar sync)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the constructed evt sets destinationCalendar to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exist (`... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events it tries to add team members' calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, so any collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are never added, meaning the event won't be created on those team members' destination calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts ~line 985-995: user.destinationCalendar assumed present but loadUsers for dynamic events selects ...userSelect.select, credentials, metadata — if destinationCalendar isn't in userSelect.select member calendars are silently skipped; also loadUsers catch converts any error into a 500 'Unable to load users', masking root causes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a broad try/catch around `loadUsers` in `handleNewBooking.ts` that will rethrow non-`HttpError` / non-`PrismaClientKnownRequestError` failures as a generic 500 `HttpError({ message: "Unable to load users" })`, which can mask underlying causes and reduce debuggability. However, the claim that `user.destinationCalendar` is "assumed present" and that member calendars are skipped because `destinationCalendar` isn’t selected cannot be verified from this diff: `userSelect.select` is not shown here, and the new code guards `if (... && user.destinationCalendar)` rather than assuming it exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts createEvent ~line 145-147: if no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, event is silently inserted into 'primary' instead of the user's selected calendar, creating events in the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). This is a behavior change that can create events in the wrong calendar when `destinationCalendar` does not include an entry with the current `credentialId` (e.g., entries missing `credentialId`, or mismatched arrays), and it is “silent” (no error/log). The diff shows multiple paths where `destinationCalendar` can be an array without guaranteed `credentialId` matches (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` branch where `destination.credentialId` is absent and it iterates credentials anyway), making the finding verifiable from the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: core/CalendarManager.ts createEvent: only Google's createEvent signature accepts credentialId; for Lark/O365/Base the find-by-credentialId matching doesn't work and collective multi-calendar creates still write every member's event to destinationCalendar[0], creating the same event N times into the main host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` to loop over every destination and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts). However, only Google’s service actually selects the calendar based on the credential (`GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` finds `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), while Lark/O365/BaseCalendarService still derive the calendarId from the *first* entry only (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). Since `createAllCalendarEvents` passes the same `event` object (with destinationCalendar array) for each destination, non-Google integrations will repeatedly target `destinationCalendar[0]`, causing incorrect calendar selection and potentially duplicating/inserting all events into the main host’s calendar (or failing if that externalId isn’t valid for that credential).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts createEvent ~line 121-124: 'main host' attendee email taken from destinationCalendar[0], which for collective bookings depends on push order and may not be the actual organizer, so attendees see wrong organizer identity

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent`, the organizer attendee email is derived from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email` (around the shown lines 115-124). But event insertion now supports multiple destination calendars (see `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterating over `event.destinationCalendar` and calling `createEvent` for each destination/credential). For any non-first destination, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` may not correspond to the calendar/credential currently being used for insertion (even though `calendarId` selection correctly uses `.find(cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). This mismatch can cause the event payload to attribute the organizer attendee email to the wrong destination calendar identity for collective/team multi-calendar cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents: DB-fetched credential with null app.slug is silently skipped — no error, no result entry, booking succeeds with missing calendar sync

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has `credentialId` but the credential isn’t in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it from DB and only constructs `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` (see the `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) { credential = { appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug, ... } }` block). If the DB record exists but `app.slug` is null/undefined, `credential` stays undefined and the subsequent `if (credential) { ... createEvent ... }` is skipped with no error and no failure `EventResult` entry, meaning calendar sync can be silently missing while the booking flow continues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts ~line 1871-1876: only destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the booking record, so downstream code (confirm, cancel, payments) only sees one calendar and may miss others when reconstructing evt

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and, in `handleNewBooking.ts`, explicitly pushes additional team destination calendars for COLLECTIVE team events (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` (the first element) via Prisma (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`). Downstream handlers shown in the diff (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, cancel/payment/webhook handlers) reconstruct `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) into a one-element array, so any additional destination calendars added at booking creation time are not recoverable from the booking record. This can lead to missing calendar event creation/updates for those additional calendars in flows that rebuild `evt` from the booking (notably confirmation/payment flows).
